clue.text: See unruly boy initially on cart flipped, streaking round

indicators.note: flipped means turned over, so the whole string built from the earlier words is read backwards

parts.note: to see something, as in 'I can see you're tired', is to tell

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words that precede it

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch a wild lad riding on an overturned cart as it hurtles round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' reverses TELL + UB + RE + CART as one string. Tracer Bullet is the hard-boiled private-eye alter ego of Calvin in Calvin and Hobbes, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A round is a single bullet, and a tracer leaves a glowing streak so its path can be seen.

clue.text: Stuffed article is lifelike

indicators.note: something stuffed has been crammed and squashed out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A taxidermy specimen in a museum looks convincingly alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffed' looks like taxidermy describing the article, but it signals the anagram of ARTICLE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something realistic is true to life, the synonym of lifelike.

clue.text: Pristine cold slope

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
to lean is to slope or tilt

explanation.surface: A spotless, chilly hillside, perhaps fresh snow on a ski run.
explanation.definitionFit: Pristine means spotless and untouched, a close synonym.

clue.text: Drew strips with live large cat rising

indicators.note: strips means the word Drew is stripped of its outer letters, leaving its core

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the lion is the big cat

explanation.surface: A cartoonist sketched comic strips showing a big cat coming to life and getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strips' looks like comic strips that Drew drew, but it means stripping DREW of its first and last letters to leave RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is an uprising or revolt, the same thing as an armed rebellion.

clue.text: Revolting bug an extract from paper lunch container?

indicators.note: revolting suggests rebellion and upheaval, so these letters are overturned and rearranged

explanation.surface: A disgusting insect is pulled out of a brown-paper lunch bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' reads as disgusting but signals the anagram of BUG AN. The definition is a verb phrase, so the answer is a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbag something is to take it out of its bag, here a paper sack holding lunch.

clue.text: They're rough in the bath, spreading flash floods centrally

indicators.note: spreading means the letters are scattered and laid out again in a new order
centrally takes the two middle letters of the word floods

explanation.surface: A sudden flood in a bathroom has spread the water everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges FLASH together with OO, the centre of FLOODS.
explanation.definitionFit: Loofahs are coarse, dried-gourd sponges used for scrubbing the skin in the bath.

clue.text: Birdsong way up entertains pair on front of Weirdos From Another Planet

indicators.note: entertains means holds a guest inside, so one piece is placed within the other
in a down clue, up means the letters of the street abbreviation are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
the pair of letters at the front of the word Weirdos
ET is the extra-terrestrial, a being from another planet

explanation.surface: Odd creatures from space are serenaded by birds, nodding to the Calvin and Hobbes book Weirdos From Another Planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the reversal and 'entertains' the container. 'pair on front of' takes two letters, not one. Weirdos From Another Planet! is a Calvin and Hobbes collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweets are the chirps of small birds, the sound of birdsong.

clue.text: Club leader cheers, elected with hat on

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the hat sits above the rest, coming first

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat
TA is British slang for thanks, like cheers
a candidate who has been elected is in

explanation.surface: A sports club's chief celebrates winning an election, still wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is a casual British word for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: The captain is the leader of a sports team or club side.

clue.text: Tigerish second character in silly comedy becoming live regularly

indicators.note: becoming means one part turns into another, so a letter is replaced

parts.note: a farce is a silly, knockabout comedy
the second letter of the comedy word

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of live, its second and fourth

explanation.surface: A tiger shows up in a madcap comedy that is broadcast live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' swaps the second letter of FARCE, A, for IE, taken from 'live' by 'regularly'. Hobbes, the tiger, is Calvin's friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigerish means savage and ferocious, as a tiger is, so it matches fierce.

clue.text: Make cartoon of endlessly manic couple

indicators.note: endlessly drops both ends of the word manic, leaving its middle

parts.note: to couple, as animals do, is to mate

explanation.surface: A frenzied pair become the subject of a cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate something is to turn it into a moving cartoon.

clue.text: Comic jump on sleigh ending in catastrophe

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the jump comes after the sleigh

parts.note: a bob is short for a bobsleigh
to hop is to jump

indicators.note: ending in takes the final letter of catastrophe

explanation.surface: Someone leaps onto a sledge and it all ends in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Hope was a British-born American comedian and film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Hope was a famous comedian, so a comic is a fair description of him.

clue.text: Twisty sliding around on trails around Ohio

indicators.note: the second around means the shuffled letters go round the state abbreviation
sliding around suggests things slipping out of place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is used as a short form for the US state of Ohio

explanation.surface: A winding route has walkers slipping and sliding on muddy trails in Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sliding around' rearranges ON TRAILS, and the second 'around' wraps that round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsional relates to torsion, twisting force, so it describes something twisty.

clue.text: Stupendous Man a little gingerly opposed to cycling

indicators.note: a little of the word gingerly is just its opening letter
cycling means letters go round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: A superhero gingerly declines to ride a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the A of ANTI to the end, giving IANT. Stupendous Man is Calvin's caped superhero alter ego in Calvin and Hobbes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupendous man is a huge, mighty figure, which a giant is.

clue.text: Imagine pterodactyl eats without finesse

indicators.note: eats means the words take something in, so the answer is held inside them

explanation.surface: Picture a pterodactyl eating with terrible table manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy and lacking skill, so it describes acting with no finesse.

clue.text: Painful blow from cat, with it left in laundry

indicators.note: in places the fashionable word and the abbreviation inside the laundry word

parts.note: the wash is the laundry
hip, like with it, means fashionable

explanation.surface: A cat swipes painfully at someone who has put it into the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' is not the pet but the cat-o'-nine-tails, a many-tailed whip once used for flogging.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, and a lash from it is a painful stroke of the whip.

clue.text: Sort of snow aimer, one regularly going for people like Susie?

definitions.text: one regularly going for people like Susie?

indicators.note: sort means put in order, so these letters are sorted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Calvin aims snowballs at Susie, his neighbour, in Calvin and Hobbes.
explanation.walkthrough: Susie Derkins is the girl Calvin pesters in Calvin and Hobbes; 'going for' means chasing, not attacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser habitually chases women, and Susie is a girl, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Son wearing close-fitting material raised 18 20's arms

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the whole string is read upwards

parts.note: snug means fitting closely

indicators.note: wearing means having something on, so the son sits inside the material word

parts.note: material, as in material evidence, means real

explanation.surface: A boy wears tight clothing and raises his toy weapons, as Calvin does when playing his space hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses SNUG + RESAL. Spaceman Spiff (18 and 20) is Calvin's space-explorer fantasy self.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaceman Spiff fights aliens with ray weapons, so laser guns are his armaments.

clue.text: Duff toy destroyed at leisure

indicators.note: destroyed means broken up, so these letters are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A useless toy gets wrecked during playtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone off duty is not working, so they are free and at leisure.

clue.text: Alien son emptied boxes despite what mom said

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the outer pair surrounds the rest
emptied means the word son loses its insides, keeping only the outside letters

parts.note: pace is Latin for with due respect to, used before naming someone you disagree with; Ma is Mom, so pace Ma means despite what Mom said

explanation.surface: A boy hollows out cardboard boxes to play aliens, ignoring his mother's orders.
explanation.walkthrough: PACE (said PAH-chay) is a formal word meaning 'with respect to', placed before someone whose view you are about to contradict.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceman in science fiction may be a visitor from another world, an alien.

clue.text: Rustic green food mushed up, mutant leaving upset stomach

parts.note: mushy peas are a British dish of mashed green peas

indicators.note: leaving means those letters go out of the word mutant
in a down clue, upset means the letters are turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: tum is a childish word for stomach

explanation.surface: A boy refuses mashed green vegetables, saying they made a mutant's stomach turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TUM into MUT, and 'leaving' removes MUT from MUTANT to leave ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic is a country dweller, a farm labourer or peasant.

clue.text: Small boy doing tiger training belted out "SMARTEN UP"

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
Pi is the boy who shares a lifeboat with a tiger in the novel Life of Pi
FF, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud, as a song belted out

explanation.surface: A little lad training his tiger bellows an order at it to tidy itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Spiff is also Calvin's space-hero name (Spaceman Spiff).
explanation.definitionFit: To spiff, usually spiff up, is to make smart, to smarten up.

clue.text: Bicipital iceman keeps leaning to the right

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the answer is kept inside these words

explanation.surface: A muscular frozen man leans rightwards, perhaps a bodybuilder snowman.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes to the right, so it is lettering that leans that way.

clue.text: Boy going around with buddy admitted burning gel

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue, going around means the word for boy is turned round

parts.note: a boy grows into a man; here man is used for boy
a pal is a buddy

explanation.surface: A lad walking about with his friend is let in somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' signals the reversal and 'admitted' the container; 'Boy' standing for a man is a loose but common crossword equation.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm is a jellied incendiary used in firebombs, a burning gel.

clue.text: Bedlam as snowball stocks accumulate

indicators.note: stocks means has in stock, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: Chaos breaks out as a snowball fight builds up supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather a large quantity, to accumulate.

clue.text: Dad's initial contribution that might be counted in performance assessment?

definitions.text: Dad's initial contribution that might be counted in performance assessment?

parts.words: Dad's initial contribution that might be counted in performance assessment?
parts.note: a father's first part in making a child, and a fertility test checks its count

explanation.surface: A father's early efforts are judged in an appraisal at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance assessment' sounds like a job review, but the count meant is the one taken in a fertility test.
explanation.definitionFit: A father's first contribution to a baby is biological, the male cells counted in a fertility test.

clue.text: It's A Magical World that can't be put down

parts.note: never means at no time, so what will never happen can't be
to land something is to put it down, as a plane on a runway

explanation.surface: A book about a fantasy world so gripping you cannot stop reading it.
explanation.walkthrough: It's a Magical World is the title of the last Calvin and Hobbes collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan's island, where children never grow up, is a magical make-believe world.

clue.text: Woman stitching up tiger, perhaps child's bloomer

parts.note: a vet is someone who treats animals, such as stitching a wounded tiger
CH is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A woman sews up a child's toy tiger, as Calvin's mother might mend Hobbes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder or an old garment, but here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Vetch is a flowering plant of the pea family, so it is a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Story of prodigious brat produced in America repeatedly

indicators.note: in places the word for produced inside the two abbreviations

parts.note: America is abbreviated twice over: A, then US
made means produced

explanation.surface: A spoilt child prodigy's tale is made in the USA, one film after another.
explanation.walkthrough: Amadeus is Peter Shaffer's play, later a film, about Mozart, shown as a gifted but childish genius.
explanation.definitionFit: The play portrays the prodigy Mozart as brattish, so it is the story of a prodigious brat.

clue.text: Traveller's time elsewhere interrupted by teacher coming over

indicators.note: interrupted by means something breaks into the middle of the word for elsewhere

parts.note: someone who is out is elsewhere, not at home

indicators.note: coming over means the teacher's title is turned round

parts.note: Sir is how pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: A traveller's holiday abroad is cut short when a teacher visits.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is a person on a sightseeing trip, a kind of traveller.

clue.text: Transmogrify mom to reshape faults

indicators.note: faults, as in geological faults, break and shift layers, so these letters are displaced

explanation.surface: A child asks a magic spell to change Mom so as to correct her flaws.
explanation.walkthrough: Transmogrify is Calvin's word: his cardboard box transmogrifier turns him into animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to change form completely, often magically, so they are synonyms.
